title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
abstract: arXiv:2610.27027v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. translated_title: 多智能体协作能否减少临床任务中的幻觉？
translated_abstract: 多智能体LLM系统在临床任务上提升了性能，这种提升常被解读为系统更值得信赖的证据。然而，这两者并非同一命题。临床医生依据的是系统所陈述的推理过程而不仅仅是结论，因此协作是否减少幻觉、以及何时减少由什么决定，也必须对推理过程进行度量。然而，大多数评估只对最终答案进行打分。我们评估了四个系统（一个单LLM基线和三种多智能体拓扑结构），覆盖四个模型和三个临床任务，在事实性与忠实性分类体系下，对每个系统生成的推理依据中的幻觉进行打分，并将其与任务指标一同报告。我们发现，协作能够换取任务性能，但并不必然带来更低的幻觉，且没有任何一种拓扑结构能够稳定地优于其他拓扑。这种效应因模型而异：在36个模型-系统-任务组合的比较中，有12个的差异大到足以分辨……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次在临床任务的推理过程中（而非仅最终答案）评估幻觉，发现多智能体协作虽能提升任务性能，但并不必然降低幻觉，且效果因模型和拓扑结构而异。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates hallucination within the generated reasoning of clinical LLM systems rather than only final answers, showing that multi-agent collaboration improves task performance but does not generally reduce hallucination, with effects varying by model and topology.
